scope: Official documentation plus CPU index links and wheel HEAD only; proposed CI-only installation step, not executed.

official_sources.finding: Official installation selector provides CPU builds on Linux and Windows; Linux support requires glibc >=2.28. The selector was not used to infer exact 2.14.1 wheel availability.
Official Linux and Windows CPU installation examples use --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu.
When an equality specifier uses a public version without a local suffix, a candidate local-version suffix is ignored for matching.
Index exposes the required 2.14.1+cpu cp312-cp312 Windows amd64 and manylinux_2_28 x86_64 wheel links.

placement: After setuptools install and before python -m pip install -r requirements-lock.txt
limitations: HEAD confirms object availability at retrieval time, not wheel integrity; the SHA-256 fragments are published index metadata and were not independently verified against wheel bytes.
Neither pip resolution nor installation nor hosted Windows/Linux tests were executed; CPU-index dependency resolution and transitive compatibility remain untested.
This does not prove the exact dependency metadata of the default-PyPI torch wheel. The proposal chooses the explicit CPU variant to avoid selecting a CUDA-enabled build.
The Linux wheel requires glibc >=2.28 and x86_64. The GitHub ubuntu-latest alias can change; CI execution is still needed.
The CPU wheel payload remains approximately 196 MB on Linux and 124 MB on Windows. No installation time or hosted-run success guarantee is made.
This CI-specific build choice does not establish parity with the frozen research runtime signature and must not be treated as authorization to resume research fits under a changed environment.
